questions.q:
A network transmits 15 packets. Each packet has a 0.92 probability of successful delivery. What is the probability that **exactly 14 packets** are delivered successfully?

Use: $P(X = x) = \binom{n}{x} p^x (1-p)^{n-x}$
A software testing team runs 20 test cases. Historical data shows 30% of test cases reveal bugs. What is the probability that **exactly 6** test cases reveal bugs?

A software testing team runs 20 test cases where each has a 30% chance of revealing a bug. What is the probability that **at least 5** test cases reveal bugs?

Hint: $P(X \geq 5) = 1 - P(X < 5)$
A cloud server has a 0.99 probability of being available during any given hour. Over a **24-hour period**, what is the probability that the server is available for **all 24 hours**?
An email spam filter correctly identifies spam with **95% accuracy**. If 12 spam emails arrive, what is the probability that the filter correctly identifies **at least 10** of them?
A system allows 8 login attempts, each with a **0.15 probability** of being a brute-force attack. What is the probability that **exactly 2** attempts are attacks?

A distributed database processes 50 queries, each with a **0.98 probability** of successful execution. What is the **expected number** of successful queries and the probability that **all 50 succeed**?

Select the option that correctly states both values.
questions.explanation:
**Expected value:** $E(X) = np = 50 \times 0.98 = 49$

**All 50 succeed:**
$$P(X = 50) = \binom{50}{50}(0.98)^{50}(0.02)^0 = (0.98)^{50} = 0.3642$$
So the expected successes = **49** and $P(\text{all succeed}) \approx$ **36.42%**.

questions.q:
A mobile device attempts to connect to Wi-Fi **10 times**, each with a **0.70 probability** of success. What is the probability of **fewer than 6** successful connections?

Hint: $P(X < 6) = P(X \leq 5) = \sum_{x=0}^{5} \binom{10}{x}(0.70)^x(0.30)^{10-x}$
A mobile app makes **25 API calls**, each with a **0.96 probability** of success. What is the probability that **at most 2 calls fail** (i.e., at least 23 succeed)?

A packet-switched network link has a capacity of **1 Mbps**. There are 35 users, each requiring **100 kbps** when active. Users are active only **10%** of the time. What is the probability that **more than 10 users** are simultaneously active (exceeding capacity)?
questions.explanation:
Given $n = 35$, $p = 0.10$. Network capacity is exceeded when more than 10 users are active simultaneously.

$$P(X > 10) = 1 - P(X \leq 10)$$

Using the binomial CDF: $P(X \leq 10) = 0.9996$

$$P(X > 10) = 1 - 0.9996 = \mathbf{0.0004}$$

This demonstrates that packet switching efficiently supports more users than circuit switching.

questions.q:
A DevOps team deploys code to **18 microservices**, each with a **0.88 probability** of success. Which of the following correctly states the **mean** and **standard deviation** of successful deployments?

Use: $\mu = np$ and $\sigma = \sqrt{npq}$
Continuing from the previous problem ($n=18$, $p=0.88$): What is the probability that **exactly 16 deployments** succeed?

A web server receives an average of **12 requests per second**. Assuming a Poisson distribution, what is the probability that **exactly 10 requests** arrive in a given second?

Use: $P(X = x) = \dfrac{\lambda^x e^{-\lambda}}{x!}$
A data center experiences an average of **3 hardware failures per month**. What is the probability that **no failures** occur in a given month?
questions.explanation:
Given $\lambda = 3$, $x = 0$:
$$P(X = 0) = \frac{3^0 \cdot e^{-3}}{0!} = e^{-3} = 0.04979 \approx \mathbf{0.0498}$$
The probability of zero failures is approximately **4.98%**.

questions.q:
A data center experiences an average of **3 hardware failures per month**. What is the probability of **more than 5 failures** in a given month?

Hint: $P(X > 5) = 1 - P(X \leq 5)$
A cybersecurity system detects an average of **8 suspicious activities per hour**. What is the probability of detecting **exactly 5** suspicious activities in a given hour?
Connection requests arrive at a database pool at an average rate of **20 per minute**. What is the probability that **exactly 18 connection requests** arrive in a given minute?
questions.explanation:
Given $\lambda = 20$, $x = 18$:
$$P(X = 18) = \frac{20^{18} \cdot e^{-20}}{18!} = \frac{1.048576 \times 10^{23} \times 2.061 \times 10^{-9}}{6.402 \times 10^{15}} = \mathbf{0.0844}$$
The probability is approximately **8.44%**.

questions.q:
A corporate email server receives **150 emails per hour**. What is the **expected number of emails** in a **20-minute** window, and what is the probability of receiving **exactly 45 emails** in that window?

Select the option that correctly states both values.
questions.explanation:
**Expected emails in 20 min:**
$$\lambda = 150 \times \frac{20}{60} = 50 \text{ emails}$$

**Probability of exactly 45 emails** (using logarithms for large $\lambda$):
$$\ln P(X=45) = 45\ln(50) - 50 - \ln(45!)$$
$$P(X = 45) = \mathbf{0.0483}$$
Probability ≈ **4.83%**.

questions.q: A software project receives an average of **4.5 bug reports per week**. What is the probability of receiving **exactly 6 bug reports** next week?

A software project receives an average of **4.5 bug reports per week**. What is the probability of **fewer than 3 bug reports**?

Hint: $P(X < 3) = P(X=0) + P(X=1) + P(X=2)$
An API endpoint averages **2.5 requests per minute** during off-peak hours. What is the probability of **zero requests** in a given minute?
questions.explanation:
Given $\lambda = 2.5$, $x = 0$:
$$P(X = 0) = \frac{2.5^0 \cdot e^{-2.5}}{0!} = e^{-2.5} = \mathbf{0.0821}$$
The probability of zero requests is **8.21%**.

questions.q:
A storage system performs an average of **180 I/O operations per minute**. Using the **normal approximation**, what is the probability of **exactly 200 I/O operations** occurring in a minute?

Use continuity correction: $P(X=200) \approx P(199.5 < X < 200.5)$
questions.explanation:
Given $\lambda = 180$, using normal approximation:
- $\mu = 180$, $\sigma = \sqrt{180} = 13.416$

With continuity correction:
$$z_1 = \frac{199.5 - 180}{13.416} = 1.454, \quad z_2 = \frac{200.5 - 180}{13.416} = 1.528$$

$$P(X=200) \approx \Phi(1.528) - \Phi(1.454) \approx \mathbf{0.0166}$$

questions.q:
A storage system performs **180 I/O operations per minute** on average. Using the normal approximation, what is the probability of **at least 190 operations**?

Use continuity correction: $P(X \geq 190) \approx P\left(Z > \frac{189.5 - 180}{\sqrt{180}}\right)$
A network monitoring system detects an average of **6 anomalies per day**. What is the probability of detecting **exactly 4 anomalies** tomorrow?

A network monitoring system detects an average of **6 anomalies per day**. Management sets an alert threshold at **8 or more** anomalies. What is the probability the alert is triggered on a given day?

Hint: $P(X \geq 8) = 1 - P(X \leq 7)$
questions.explanation:
Given $\lambda = 6$:
$$P(X \leq 7) = \sum_{x=0}^{7} \frac{6^x e^{-6}}{x!} = 0.7440$$

$$P(X \geq 8) = 1 - 0.7440 = \mathbf{0.2560}$$
The alert is triggered with probability **25.60%**.

questions.q: A network monitoring system detects an average of **6 anomalies per day**, following a Poisson process. What is the **expected number of anomalies** over a **5-day period**?
questions.explanation:
For a Poisson process, the rate scales linearly with time:
$$\lambda_{5\text{ days}} = 6 \times 5 = \mathbf{30} \text{ anomalies}$$
This follows directly from the additive property of the Poisson distribution: if $X_i \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda)$ independently, then $\sum_{i=1}^{n} X_i \sim \text{Poisson}(n\lambda)$.

questions.q:
A web server receives **1000 queries per day** on average. The operations team wants **95% confidence** the server can meet demand. What minimum capacity (number of queries) should the server be designed to handle?

*(Find $k$ such that $P(X \leq k) \geq 0.95$)*
questions.explanation:
For a Poisson distribution with large $\lambda$, the normal approximation can also be used:
$$z_{0.95} = 1.645 \Rightarrow k \approx \mu + z \cdot \sigma = 1000 + 1.645\sqrt{1000} \approx 1052$$
Both exact and approximate methods yield $k = 1052$, providing **52 queries of excess capacity** to ensure 95% reliability.
questions.answer:
Using the Poisson cumulative distribution with $\lambda = 1000$:

$$P(X \leq 1051) = 0.9483 < 0.95$$
$$P(X \leq 1052) = 0.9507 > 0.95$$

Therefore $k = \mathbf{1052}$ queries.

Excess capacity needed: $1052 - 1000 = 52$ queries.
